cards.explanation: The answer is to welcome her and help with anything she needs, friends. Paul says, "Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you" (Romans 16:2). Phoebe is a servant of the church in Cenchrea, and Paul wants her treated right. Whatever she needs, the believers in Rome are to pitch in. That's a good rule for any kitchen, too.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says Phoebe "…has been a great help to many people, including me" (Romans 16:2). So Paul is one of many people she has helped. That's a servant of the church in Cenchrea for you, and her helping reaches well past one man.

The answer is to turn away from them, friends. Paul says to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles contrary to the teaching they have learned, and then he adds, "Turn away from them" (Romans 16:17). It's short and it's plain. No long speech needed, and I'm the one with a mustache to spare.

The answer is their own appetites, friends. Paul says such people "…are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites" (Romans 16:18). Their hearts are pointed at what they want instead of at Christ. That's a serious thing, and Paul says it plainly.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive" (Romans 16:18). There's no shouting or threatening in the verse. The danger he describes is sweet words that sound nice.

The answer is that everyone has heard about their obedience, friends. Paul writes, "Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you" (Romans 16:19). The news about the believers in Rome had spread. Paul heard it, and it made him glad. Imagine your good name traveling farther than you do.

The answer is evil, friends. Paul says, "But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil" (Romans 16:19). So he wants them wise about the good and innocent about the evil. Know the good well, and keep clear of the evil.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet" (Romans 16:20). The one doing the crushing is the God of peace. I'll tell you, I find that comforting. I spent years in the dark, and I know a promise like that hits different.

The answer is that Tertius is the one who wrote down this letter, friends. Tertius says it himself: "I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord" (Romans 16:22). When he writes "I," it's his own voice breaking into Paul's letter. I think it's a nice touch that the one holding the pen gets to say hello.

The answer is hosting the whole church, friends. Paul says Gaius "…has hosted me and all the church…" (Romans 16:23). That's Paul and the whole church that Gaius hosted. I can barely handle a few bakers crowding my counter, so I'm impressed.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says the mystery was "concealed for ages past but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets" (Romans 16:25-26). The key word is "now." What was hidden has been made known, so it's out of the oven and on the table.

The answer is nations, friends. Paul says the mystery is made known "…in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith…" (Romans 16:26). Not just one nation, but all of them. That's a wide reach for a message.

The answer is through Jesus Christ, friends. Paul closes with, "…to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen" (Romans 16:27). That's how he ends the whole letter, with glory to God forever through Jesus Christ. It's a mighty good last line.
